title: No Root Edit may take the Osero Artifact outside the Sky Core Atlas, and the Facilitator must enforce that limit
content:
A.6.1.1.7.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.6, Artifact Edit Restrictions, states: "The Osero Artifact cannot be edited in any way that violates the Sky Core Atlas or its specifications of the Sky Primitives, or in any way that is otherwise misaligned. The Operational Facilitator must enforce this rule through their review of Artifact Edit Proposals."

This establishes a hierarchy of norms. The Artifact is subordinate legislation; the Sky Core Atlas is the constitution. OSERO token holders control the Artifact's content only within the space the Atlas leaves open, so a unanimous holder vote cannot authorize an Atlas-violating edit.

The restriction has three branches, and the third is the widest. Violating the Atlas and violating its Primitive specifications are relatively checkable; "otherwise misaligned" is an open-textured standard with no enumerated test. That is consistent with the Atlas's spirit-of-the-rule doctrine, but it means the Facilitator's veto rests partly on a criterion that cannot be litigated against a text.

Enforcement is also placed entirely inside the review stage rather than at execution or afterwards. There is no described mechanism for reversing an Atlas-violating edit that slipped through review — the guarantee is only as strong as the gate at A.6.1.1.7.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.3.
description: Prime Governance is bounded, not sovereign: edits violating the Atlas, its Primitive specifications, or alignment generally are void regardless of how many OSERO holders approve them.
